trial_court: Principal Judge, Family Court, Jhansi (Case No.205 of 2011 and Case No.94 of 2011)
case_name: Smt. Monika Gupta vs Jitendra Gandhi
facts_of_case: Appellant filed cases under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act for annulling marriage on grounds of constant demand for dowry by in-laws and not being treated well. Respondent filed case under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act for restitution of conjugal rights.

legal_principles.principle: Mental cruelty can be defined as conduct which inflicts mental pain and suffering that makes it not possible for the parties to live together.
legal_principles.held: Mental cruelty must be of such a nature that the parties cannot reasonably be expected to live together. The situation must be such that the wronged party cannot reasonably be asked to put up with such conduct and continue to live with the other party.
cited_cases: V. Bhagat Vs. D. Bhagat, (1994) 1 SCC 337

legal_principles.principle: Cruelty can be established without physical violence.
legal_principles.held: Continuous ill-treatment, cessation of marital intercourse, studied neglect, indifference on the part of the husband, and an assertion on the part of the husband that the wife is unchaste are all factors which may undermine the health of a wife.
cited_cases: Sirajmohmedkhan Janmohamadkhan Vs. Hafizunnisa Yasinkhan and another, (1981) 4 SCC 250

outcome.final_order: The trial court's order was set aside, and the marriage was annulled.
